Now: 'fair of skin and with beautiful hair'. 'Back in Rome, says Bede' is also removed. Bede gives no date. The Whitby Life puts the story under Pope Benedict I (574 to 578), before Constantinople. Numbers: Bede 1.25's 'nearly forty men' is the party that LANDED on Thanet, with Frankish interpreters picked up on the way. The chip changed from 'Sent to the English' to 'Landed in Kent'. The monasteries line now follows its cited source, Gregory of Tours: 'a seventh within the Roman walls'. The page had said 'family home'.

Miracles lede, three fixes. (1) 'No one of his own time records a miracle by him' is a claim that nothing exists, and no source says it. Justus, the dark panel: Dialogues Book 4, chapter 55 says it 'happened three years since in mine own Monastery', and the Dialogues were written about 593 to 594. The date changed from 'Before 590' to 'About 590'.

Trait 'patient until pushed': Maximus was ordained against the EMPEROR's orders (Letter 4.47: 'the most serene Lord the Emperor had sent orders that he should not be ordained'). The page said 'against his orders'. The letter is to Sabinian, his envoy, so 'Gregory warned' became 'Gregory wrote to his envoy'.

Trait 'no grand titles': Letter 8.30 says 'my honour is the honour of the universal Church: my honour is the solid vigour of my brethren'. The page said 'the honour of his brother bishops'. Now: 'the honour of the whole Church and the strength of his brothers'.

Hard parts, Mary Magdalene: 22 July has been a feast, not a memorial, since 2016. Now: 'Its day for her, 22 July, is for Mary Magdalene alone.' I checked the Homily 33 identification in Migne PL 76 and the 1969 Calendarium note. Slavery: Letter 6.7 says boys 'of about seventeen or eighteen'. The page now says 'about'.

Circle, Theodelinda: Paul the Deacon Book 4, chapter 6 does not support 'worked through her for peace'. The cite is now Book 4, chapter 5 plus Letters, Book 14, letter 12 ('move his mind to peace, as you have been accustomed to do').
